Method of Attack: UEFI bootkit malware capable of evading detection, withstanding removal efforts, and neutralizing multiple Windows security features such as Defender, HVCI, and BitLocker
Exploits Secure Boot zero-day vulnerability CVE-2023-24932 and CVE-2022-21894 (Baton Drop) to bypass Secure Boot protections
Deploys an older EFI binary of the Windows boot loader onto the boot partition
Disables BitLocker and Memory Integrity protections before implanting malware
Targets earliest software stage of boot, not firmware
Removes Secure Boot policy enforcement by exploiting vulnerable boot loaders not revoked in Secure Boot DBX
Attack Vector: Exploitation of Secure Boot vulnerabilities in Windows boot loaders (CVE-2022-21894 and CVE-2023-24932)
Installation via vulnerable boot loaders that bypass Secure Boot protections
Deployment of malicious EFI binary on boot partition
Indicators of Compromise: Use of older Extensible Firmware Interface (EFI) binary of Windows boot loader on boot partition
Disabling of BitLocker and Memory Integrity protections prior to reboot
Presence of vulnerable boot loaders not revoked in Secure Boot Deny List Database (DBX)
